name: Miro
summary: Visual collaboration platform: an infinite online whiteboard for brainstorms, diagrams, workshops and planning — with templates, voting and AI that generates diagrams and summaries, built for real-time and async teamwork.
best_for: teams that think visually — brainstorms, flowcharts, retros, workshops and planning on an infinite shared canvas with strong templates and facilitation tools
skip_if: your work is mostly documents or task tracking (a doc or PM tool fits better) or most of your company would only ever need to view, not edit
honest_knock: Per-member pricing charges for every member added to the workspace, so an org-wide rollout multiplies at full headcount — and the free plan's cap of 3 editable boards is workspace-wide, not per person. In our test on 20 October 2026 Miro did not block a fourth board: it warned that the oldest board would become view-only, and a new free team already starts with one board made for you. Model who truly needs to edit before you buy seats.

pricing.notes: (price re-verified 2026-09-23 on miro.com/pricing/) Free plan: 3 editable boards workspace-wide, unlimited members, AI shown as a limited trial in the plan table, which the FAQ puts at 10 credits a month. Starter $8/member/mo and Business $20/member/mo, both billed yearly; Enterprise custom priced from 30 members. The yearly toggle is marked save 20%, which puts the monthly rates at $10 and $25. AI credits are published per plan: 25 per member per month on Starter, 50 on Business. MCP calls are a separate published meter: 500 a day on Starter, 2,000 on Business. Currency note: the served page defaults to USD, but rendered from a Dutch connection the same numerals appear as €8 and €20, so the symbol follows the visitor region. Enterprise starts from 2,500 AI credits a month, scaling with seats and pooled org-wide, and 10,000 MCP calls a day; Free gets 100 MCP calls a day. Credits are pooled across the organisation, reset monthly without rollover, and extra credit packages can be bought. Guests (free accounts invited to specific boards, no paid seat) exist only on Business and Enterprise; on Free anyone invited becomes a member. 14-day Business trial. Startups under 30 employees can get $500 or $1,000 in Miro credits.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on a new free account: Daan created the team and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser. We added five sticky notes (one by hand, four with bulk mode), aligned them, exported them to CSV and as an image, and created boards until the free plan's limit appeared.
findings: A new free team opened with a ready-made 'My First Board' and a 'Free plan' label, so one board already counts toward the limit before you start.

Attempting a fourth board opened a warning: 'You've reached the limit of three editable boards' and 'My First Board will become view-only', with 'Create team board' and 'Upgrade'. We did not confirm creation, so we verified the warning, not the change to the old board.
The first click on '+ Create' opened a 14-day Business trial offer, which 'Maybe later' closed. Each new board said it was shared with all members of the team.
Bulk mode is not in the sticky-note menu but under + (Tools) when you search for 'bulk'. Four lines became four stickies in a 2x2 grid, smaller than a single sticky.
The Align menu has 8 options. Top-aligning the 2x2 grid stacked the stickies on top of each other, and distributing kept the old width, so the overlap stayed; that menu has no automatic spacing.
Export to CSV gave a 53-byte file (UTF-8 with BOM): one column, no header row, TEST-01 to TEST-05 once each, and no colour, position or structure.

Image export on Free offered only Small: a 2449 x 1632 px JPG of 81 kB with no visible watermark and sharp text. Medium, Large, vector PDF and SVG sat behind Upgrade, and the default export frame cut off the left edge of the first sticky.
